reason: B is the stronger, nanoparticle-specific and non-trivial extension: it tests whether a chemically altered surface overrides core SRO stabilization using matched particles, measurable premelting onset, and an explicit falsification criterion, whereas A largely restates prior SRO–thermal-stability work. Its main weakness is that oxidation may instead form a refractory shell and air treatment introduces interfacial-phase confounders, so surface segregation and oxidation should ideally be tested separately.
